items.name: saga
items.author: warpdotdev
items.description: Support build phase development with Claude Code
items.summary: Saga is an orchestrator skill for medium-to-large feature implementation using a three-phase workflow: spec planning, delegated worker execution, and final validation. The orchestrator transforms rough requirements into airtight specs with explicit validation criteria, then delegates parallelizable tasks to worker subagents while preserving its own context window. State lives in a saga directory (outside the repo) enabling resumption across sessions. Workers self-validate against contracts, commit durably, and report compactly. Human involvement is limited to spec approval and final manual acceptance. Success depends on tight task definitions and validation criteria written before any implementation begins.
highlights: Three-phase workflow: Planning (spec + approval), Execution (worker delegation + validation), Acceptance (final criteria
Spec-driven contracts with airtight validation criteria per task, preventing ambiguity and enabling parallel execution
Saga directory persists outside repo for resumption, state recovery, and multi-session coherence
Orchestrator stays lean by delegating code to workers, reading compact reports, and keeping state on disk
Git worktree isolation per task with saga-traceable branch naming (saga/<name>/m<M>t<T>-<slug>)

items.name: dbs-content-system
items.author: dontbesilent2025
items.description: Stand up and verify a structured content library that turns raw drafts and tweets into reusable units, topic maps, and publish-ready assemblies.
items.summary: The dbs-content-system skill turns large local content archives into a reusable structured engineering project instead of delivering a one-off summary. It starts in audit mode: count text files, estimate volume, classify source types, and confirm inclusion boundaries before any heavy work. Entry requires at least fifty files or eighty thousand characters and two source dimensions such as published posts, drafts, case studies, or course transcripts. After audit it scaffolds a fixed directory tree with rules, raw copy archives, unit libraries, processing state, templates, topic maps, and assembly drafts. Content is split into five unit types: QST questions, CON concepts, OPI opinions, CAS cases, and SOL solutions, each as Markdown with YAML frontmatter and Obsidian links. Work proceeds through gated modes from audit to sample to batch to full, with Node scripts for source registry, unit extraction, link maps, deduplication, and system summaries. Default delivery stops at a usable system with sample units, topic maps, and assembly drafts rather than full corpus completion.
highlights: Audits volume and boundaries before creating the engineering project.
Scaffolds a fixed 00-07 directory tree with rules and state files.
Extracts QST, CON, OPI, CAS, and SOL units with YAML frontmatter.
Runs gated audit, sample, batch, and full modes with upgrade gates.
Ships Node scripts for registry, deduplication, links, and summaries.

items.description: Teaches an agent to query on-chain canister data using OQL, a JSON query language with filters, joins, aggregation, and pagination against Internet Computer canisters.
items.summary: extension-querying-oql is a skill that lets an agent query data stored in Internet Computer canisters through OQL, a JSON-based query language supporting filtering, sorting, pagination, aggregation, and relationship traversal. A solo builder reaches for it when reading structured on-chain data through the Caffeine Data Intelligence agent, discovering schemas and forming queries without hand-writing canister calls.
highlights: JSON-based OQL query language
Filters, joins, aggregation, pagination
Schema discovery via schema()
Queries Internet Computer canisters

items.name: write-feature-docs
items.author: warpdotdev
items.description: Writes feature documentation describing what a new feature does, how it works, and how to use it, keeping docs current as features land.
items.summary: The write-feature-docs skill draft a complete documentation page for a new Warp feature from its PRODUCT.md and/or TECH.md spec. Use when an engineer has written a spec and needs to produce a first-pass MDX draft for the warpdotdev/docs repo. Also handles features without specs by researching the codebase first. Invoke this skill whenever an engineer mentions writing docs for a feature, drafting a docs page, creating feature documentation, starting the eng-docs workflow, or converting a spec into documentation. Works from w # write-feature-docs Draft a complete documentation page for a new Warp feature. You read the feature's spec, verify technical claims by researching the codebase yourself, present a concise outline for the engineer to confirm, then produce a complete MDX draft and open a draft PR in `warpdotdev/docs`  -  tagging the docs team for review. The engineer's job is to confirm what you couldn't verify from the spec and code  -  not to do a full accuracy review, not to polish prose, not to know docs conventions.
highlights: Find and read the spec files
Research the codebase to verify technical claims  -  minimize what the engineer needs to check
Generate a concise outline, distinguishing verified facts from open questions
Engineer confirms or corrects
Generate the complete MDX draft

items.name: expo-examples
items.author: expo
items.description: For development and infrastructure management.
items.summary: expo-examples is Expo's official skill for mining the expo/examples library of roughly 70 with-* integration directories such as with-stripe, with-clerk, and with-supabase. Each example is a managed single-screen project showing dependency sets, app.json config plugins, and minimal wiring maintained against the current SDK. Two modes exist: inspiration mode reads an example as reference and ports patterns non-destructively into the user's app, while scaffold mode starts a fresh project via npx create-expo --example. The workflow maps user needs to example names, confirms against the live GitHub tree and meta.json aliases or deprecated entries, then reads high-signal files: README, package.json, app.json, integration code, and .env placeholders. Adaptation rules require npx expo install for SDK-correct versions, merging only missing config plugins, and recreating env var shapes without copying secrets. Gotchas note the default branch is master and every example ships a launch.expo.dev one-click deploy URL.
highlights: ~70 official with-* integration examples (Stripe, Clerk, Supabase, maps, Skia, NativeWind).
Inspiration mode ports patterns by hand; scaffold mode uses npx create-expo --example.
Live triage via gh api plus meta.json for aliases and deprecated example redirects.
Non-destructive adaptation: expo install versions, merge config plugins, port integration code only.
Recursive tree listing and degit sparse-checkout for studying multi-file integrations.

items.name: scan-new-specs
items.author: warpdotdev
items.description: Scans a repo or workspace for new or updated spec documents so an agent picks up requirements changes and keeps implementation aligned with the latest specs.
items.summary: The scan-new-specs skill scan warpdotdev/warp and warp-server for recently merged PRODUCT.md specs that don't yet have a corresponding docs PR in warpdotdev/docs. When a complete spec is found, auto-generates a full docs draft PR and tags the engineer. When a spec is too thin to draft from, pings the engineer directly. Designed to run as a scheduled Oz ambient agent (e.g., every 2-3 days). Use when setting up the automated docs trigger or running a manual docs coverage sweep. # scan-new-specs Scan `warpdotdev/warp` and `warp-server` for recently merged product or tech specs that lack a corresponding docs draft. For each gap: - **If the spec is complete**  -  automatically run `write-feature-docs` in ambient mode to generate a full draft PR in `warpdotdev/docs`, then ping the engineer to review it - **If the spec is thin**  -  ping the engineer directly to either flesh out the spec or kick off the docs workflow manually In both cases, post a summary to `#growth-docs`.
highlights: **If the spec is complete**  -  automatically run `write-feature-docs` in ambient mode to generate a full draft PR in `w
**If the spec is thin**  -  ping the engineer directly to either flesh out the spec or kick off the docs workflow manual
File is at least 40 lines long
Contains a `## Behavior` section (or equivalent) with numbered invariants or user-facing steps
Describes at least one concrete user action (not just a summary paragraph)
